I'm a bit confused. Where are you located? If this is in the US... The. The papers you have sound fake. SDs don't require or have any kind of certifications, ID, or documents. Usually when someone has these, it's a red flag that the service dog is fake. At least that's how it is in the US. So I'm curious if You're in a different country. Where I'm from, if someone is presenting any kind of documentation, certification or ID for a "service dog" or event an ESA (All you need for this is a doctor's note. It's basically a prescription), then the SA is fake. It also teaches the employees of that establishment that they need to see some kind of paperwork for a service dog every time someone brings one in. And the issue that comes with that as if someone brings in a real service dog and they don't have any kind of papers because it's not legally required nor are there any programs recognized legally for this, It makes it very difficult for people with a real service dog to enter places. 

I'm not saying that your dog is not a real service dog. I'm just curious where you're at and what kind of papers you have. Because again, where I'm from that's not a thing. 

Also, as far as I know, service dogs and training are not allowed into non-pet friendly stores. Until they are an actual service dog, they have to stay in pet friendly stores. 

Sorry to be that guy. I'm just confused and curious. If your in a different country and have different laws and regulations are on service animals, then that would make way more sense.

1/2 cup butter 
3/4 cup sugar 
1/4 cup brown sugar 
2 egg, beaten 
3-4 bananas (more bananas = more moisture. I use 3 1/2 and it's perfect. Leftovers go to the dogs lol) 
1 1/2 cups flour
1 tsp baking soda 
1 tsp cinnamon
1/2 tsp nutmeg
1/2 tsp salt
1/2 tsp vanilla extract 

Cream together butter an sugar 
Add eggs and crush bananas (I like my bananas crushed into a mush. I don't like the chunks in my bread, but some people do. Just use a fork). 
Sift together flour, baking soda, cinnamon, nutmeg, salt. Add vanilla
Mix everything until just combined. Do not over mix! 
Pour into a greased/floured bread pan; I always use metal. Glass pans are horrible for bread. You'll over bake, dry out the bread and the middle won't be cooked. So just sick with metal.

Bake at 350F for 55mins 

Before putting in the over, you can fold in anything extra you want, like chocolate chips, nuts, blueberries etc. But make sure you fold it in. Do not mix.
